one_liner: Experimental from-scratch C++20 embedded SQL engine for Parquet/CSV files; 1.24x geomean vs DuckDB on ClickBench, but slower in total.
what_it_does: An in-process analytical SQL database built on the same model as DuckDB and SQLite. You point SQL at CSV, Parquet, JSON, Avro, Arrow, Excel or SQLite files (local, HTTP(S) or anonymous public S3), or at a single-file .slothdb store. It ships as a CLI shell, a C API (slothdb_open / slothdb_connect / slothdb_query), a ctypes-based Python package (pip install slothdb, .sql(...).fetchdf()) and an npm WASM package. It is not a drop-in DuckDB replacement: the dialect overlaps, but SQL coverage is much narrower. Parity with DuckDB on DataFusion's sqllogictest corpus was 11.4% on 2026-05-20, and the last commit message reports 18.0%.
how_it_is_fast: The base is a vectorized columnar engine (2,048-value batches) with per-row-group parallel scans. Its ClickBench wins come mostly from query-shape-specific fast paths, found in a 14,573-line physical_planner.cpp and in separate source files. They include a fused Parquet scan+aggregate, row-group min/max pruning, and a dictionary-histogram SUM/AVG that never decodes dict-encoded INT64 pages. Others are 16-way radix-partitioned per-thread hash maps for high-cardinality COUNT GROUP BY, fused LIKE '%needle%' counting over dictionaries, and top-N heap pushdown, with AVX2 intrinsics (scalar fallback) and ankerl unordered_dense maps in the hot loops. Queries that miss these shapes fall back to a generic path that the author concedes is slow: ParallelScanFilter still copies each cell with GetValue/SetValue into vector<vector<Value>> under a mutex, and the optimizer has three passes (constant folding, filter pushdown, top-N), with no cost model or join reordering.
when_to_use: Prototypes where a tiny footprint matters more than speed: the README cites a ~1-2 MB CLI, a ~1.3 MB full WASM bundle and a sub-1 MB edge build that fits Cloudflare Workers' 1 MB limit, vs ~18 MB WASM for DuckDB.

Ad-hoc single-node queries over local Parquet that match its fast shapes: ungrouped COUNT/SUM/AVG, simple low-to-medium-cardinality GROUP BY ... COUNT(*), and ORDER BY ... LIMIT N. On these its own ClickBench table shows roughly 1.3-3x over DuckDB 1.4.3.
A dashboard tailing a growing CSV log, using CREATE LIVE VIEW, which appends only the new bytes instead of rescanning the file.
Throwaway or learning use that needs Avro, Excel, SQLite or HTTP(S)/public-S3 reads without installing extensions.
when_not_to_use: Correctness-sensitive work in place of DuckDB. Commits in May-June 2026 fixed many silent wrong-result bugs: 3-way JOIN chains dropped the middle table, multi-condition equi-joins dropped every conjunct after the first, DECIMAL columns stored 0, and computed LIMIT expressions were ignored. Only 650 of 5,720 sqllogictest queries matched DuckDB on 2026-05-20.

High-cardinality multi-column GROUP BY. ClickBench Q31 and Q32 run at 0.22x and 0.11x of DuckDB's speed, and Q19 and Q33 time out at 120 s. The source says the generic aggregator uses about 400+ bytes per group and can run out of memory or thrash at tens of millions of groups.

Filtered aggregates and other shapes without a dedicated path. In the repo's own 10M-row Parquet suite, SUM(revenue) WHERE region = 'APAC' takes 1.44 s vs 115 ms in DuckDB (0.08x), and SlothDB wins only 6 of 16 queries (median 0.92x).

Concurrent writers, OLTP, point lookups, authenticated S3, or large UPDATE/DELETE. It has a single writer, no secondary indexes and anonymous-only S3, and runs DML serially (from the README's own list of what it does not do).

Anything that needs a maintained dependency. It has one maintainer, no commits since 2026-06-03, and all of the last 100 CI runs on main (since 2026-05-20) failed or were cancelled, with the Test step failing on both Windows and Linux.

integration.form: static lib (libslothdb) by default; an optional shared lib (SLOTHDB_BUILD_SHARED) for Python and other dlopen users; also a CLI, PyPI wheels and an npm WASM package
integration.dependencies: none external. It vendors miniz, snappy, a decompression-only zstd subset, fastpforlib bitpacking, ankerl unordered_dense, linenoise and doctest. The optional .ask natural-language feature adds a llama.cpp submodule.
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 and CMake 3.14+. CI builds with MSVC (windows-latest), GCC (ubuntu-24.04) and Apple Clang (macos-13, x86_64). Python wheels need CPython 3.8+.
integration.platforms: x86-64 on Windows, Linux and macOS, with the core compiled using -mavx2 or /arch:AVX2 (the CI file also mentions BMI2 intrinsics), so pre-AVX2 CPUs are effectively unsupported. arm64 macOS and WASM builds drop AVX2 and use scalar fallbacks. Wheels exist for win_amd64, manylinux2014_x86_64 and macOS universal2, but not for Linux aarch64.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. The Catalog is mutex-protected, and the TransactionManager enforces a single writer with snapshot isolation. However, Optimizer::Optimize clears and appends to a static std::vector, so planning on two connections at once looks racy. Strings returned by the C API's catalog functions are valid only until the next call to the same function on the same thread.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: same embedded model and similar file-querying SQL (read_parquet, read_csv, FROM 'file.parquet'), and a DuckDB-like Python connect/sql/fetchdf surface. But the C API is different (slothdb_* rather than duckdb_*), SQL coverage is far narrower (the author's sqllogictest notes list arrays, structs, UNNEST and lateral joins as unsupported), and some results still differ from DuckDB's.

gotchas: The benchmark wins are shaped to the dataset. The ClickBench maintainer disqualified SlothDB (ClickHouse/ClickBench#930) after finding per-query handlers written for specific ClickBench queries, such as q4_dict_histogram.cpp and q21_helper.cpp. The author then removed four overfit hacks, two of which returned wrong results outside the benchmark, but the README says the query-shape dispatch is still in place.

The 14.81x 'win' on Q18 is GROUP BY UserID, SearchPhrase LIMIT 10 with no ORDER BY. Any 10 groups are a valid answer, and SlothDB's differs from DuckDB's, so the number mostly measures stopping early, not aggregation speed.

docs/DOCUMENTATION.md advertises automatic CUDA/Metal GPU acceleration ('20-100x faster'), but the CMake files define no SLOTHDB_CUDA or SLOTHDB_METAL option, and gpu_engine.cpp is a plain CPU fallback.
The ClickBench issue also alleges paid GitHub stars (not verified here), so the 413 stars say little about real adoption. CHANGELOG.md stops at 0.2.3 while releases have reached 0.2.7.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: For speed there is no reason to pick it over chDB (embedded ClickHouse) or DuckDB itself: it is slower than DuckDB in total ClickBench time and fails 3 of 43 queries, and for faster DuckDB-compatible execution Sirius (GPU) is the catalogued option. Pick SlothDB only when a 1-2 MB native binary or ~1 MB WASM bundle matters more than speed and correctness, or to study shape-specialized Parquet fast paths.
verified_claims_summary: Setup: the repo's official_bench.py ran the 43 verbatim ClickBench queries (DuckDB variant) on hits_typed.parquet against DuckDB v1.4.3, one fresh CLI process per trial, min of 3, 120 s timeout. The machine was a 6-core Ryzen 5 5600U laptop with 15 GB RAM on Windows 11, per a README section since removed; the script's .exe paths indicate an MSVC Release build, where CMake adds /GL /LTCG /arch:AVX2, and no compiler version is given. Result: SlothDB was faster on 29 of the 40 queries both finished (geomean 1.24x) but slower in total (71.1 s vs 65.2 s), timed out on Q19, Q29 and Q33, and returned different results on 7 queries; the earlier HN claim of '1.35x to 5x faster than DuckDB and ClickHouse' has no ClickHouse data behind it and has been withdrawn from the README.
status_note: Labelled active but single-maintainer, with no commits since 2026-06-03 and red CI since 2026-05-20; MIT-licensed and pip/npm-installable, so fine for experiments but not production.
